questions.q: What triggers the `deploy-dev` job, and what must already have happened?
options: It runs on a schedule every hour regardless of CI status
It runs on main only after the build-test-scan job has succeeded
It runs on every pull request, including from forks
A maintainer must manually click a button in the GitHub UI every time
questions.explain: The job is gated with `needs: build-test-scan` and `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, so it only runs after CI passes on a merge to main.

questions.q: How does the GitHub Actions workflow authenticate to Azure to deploy?
options: A long-lived client secret stored in GitHub Secrets
A personal access token belonging to a maintainer
An OIDC federated credential — GitHub issues a short-lived token that Azure AD exchanges for Azure access, with no stored secret
A shared password checked into the Helm chart
questions.explain: `azure/login@v2` here uses OIDC: GitHub issues a short-lived token, and Azure AD trusts it via a federated identity credential set up in Phase 2 — no client secret is stored anywhere.

questions.q: Why is `helm upgrade --install` used instead of a plain `helm install`?
options: It is idempotent — it creates the release on the first run and upgrades it on every run after, so the same command always works
It is required because Helm charts cannot be installed more than once
It skips running any Kubernetes admission controllers
It only works with the `northbridge-staging` namespace
questions.explain: `helm upgrade --install` handles both the first deploy (install) and every subsequent deploy (upgrade) with one command, which is why the same CD step works unchanged on deploy #1 or deploy #400.

questions.q: Why does `checkout`'s `values-dev.yaml` set a different autoscaling range (min 3 / max 15) than `product-catalog`'s (min 2 / max 8)?
options: It's an arbitrary difference with no operational reason
checkout handles much higher, spikier load from flash sales and needs more headroom to scale
product-catalog is written in Python, which scales differently
Helm requires every service in a monorepo to use a different range
questions.explain: checkout's load is far spikier because of flash sales, so its HorizontalPodAutoscaler is sized with a higher floor and ceiling than product-catalog's steadier read traffic.

questions.q: Why don't `values-dev.yaml`, `values-staging.yaml`, or `values-prod.yaml` ever contain the PaymentPro API key or database password directly?
options: Because Helm does not technically support string values
Because the External Secrets Operator syncs those secrets from Key Vault into Kubernetes Secrets at runtime, and the values files only reference a Secret's name
Because those secrets are hardcoded into the container image instead
Because product-catalog and checkout don't actually need any secrets
questions.explain: The External Secrets Operator, running in the cluster, pulls secrets from Key Vault into native Kubernetes Secrets that pods mount at runtime — Helm values files never hold the secret contents themselves.
